dashcam.summary:
CONTEXT SHIFT THAT DEFINES THIS SPACE: Since Tesla firmware 2025.44.25 (2025 Holiday Update, HW3+), TeslaCam embeds per-frame telemetry as SEI (Supplemental Enhancement Information) NAL units inside the H.265 video stream. Tesla published the official decoder at github.com/teslamotors/dashcam (363 stars): dashcam.proto protobuf schema, sei_extractor.py CLI, dashcam-mp4.js parser, and a drag-drop SEI Explorer web player at teslamotors.github.io/dashcam. The SeiMetadata message fields are exactly: version(uint32), gear_state(enum GEAR_PARK/DRIVE/REVERSE/NEUTRAL), frame_seq_no(uint64), vehicle_speed_mps(float), accelerator_pedal_position(float), steering_wheel_angle(float), blinker_on_left(bool), blinker_on_right(bool), brake_applied(bool), autopilot_state(enum NONE/SELF_DRIVING/AUTOSTEER/TACC), latitude_deg/longitude_deg/heading_deg(double), linear_acceleration_mps2_x/y/z(double). Note SEI has NO SOC, power, elevation, odometer, or temperature — that's the TeslaMate advantage. SEI absent when parked (Sentry clips may lack it). Second shift: firmware 2026.20 (June 2026) encrypts dashcam clips BY DEFAULT with a key tied to the Tesla account; Tesla launched dashcam.tesla.com, a web viewer that decrypts locally after Tesla-account login; encryption can be disabled in Controls > Safety > Encrypt Dashcam Recordings. Any new tool must handle encrypted clips or instruct users to disable encryption (ExportDash already does in-browser decryption).

RECORDING FORMAT: USB is exFAT (128KB clusters), TeslaCam/ root with RecentClips/ (rolling ~1h buffer, flat files), SavedClips/ and SentryClips/ (one folder per event named YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS containing the surrounding ~10 min of clips, an event.json sidecar — timestamp, city, est_lat/est_lon, reason e.g. sentry_aware_object_detection/user_interaction_dashcam_icon_tapped, camera — and thumb.png). Clips are 1-minute MP4 chunks per camera named YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS-{front|back|left_repeater|right_repeater|left_pillar|right_pillar}.mp4 (Cybertruck/Plaid add a 7th rear-backup stream). moov atom is at file END (recovery-relevant; also breaks naive progressive streaming). HW3 (4 cameras): 1280x960 all cameras, ~36 fps (measured 36.019); originally H.264, switched to HEVC/H.265 in later firmware (~2023) — the codec is firmware-dependent, not hardware-dependent, so a viewer must probe per file. HW4/AI4 (6 cameras incl. B-pillars, V10+ firmware exposes pillars): H.265; front 2896x1876 @ ~30fps (early HW4 firmware exported 1448x938 and 24fps; sources conflict 24 vs 30fps across firmware), back/left_repeater/right_repeater 1448x938 @ ~30fps; pillar cams 1448x938. HEVC breaks Chrome playback without platform HEVC decode — a recurring pain point across all web viewers.

TOOL LANDSCAPE (details in projects array): RedDash (reddash.app) is a commercial iPhone/iPad app (Pro Lifetime $9.99 or $0.99/mo, v1.2.2 Jul 2026, dev 刚 熊) plus a free browser viewer; it reads footage directly off the USB drive via Lightning/USB-C without copying, plays 4-6 cams synced, parses event.json for Sentry trigger reasons, and overlays SEI telemetry (speed, steering-angle visual, accelerator/brake, gear, AP/FSD status, GPS+heading, 3-axis accel) in a "Digital Dashboard"; export layouts: 2x2 grid, cinematic PiP, cockpit, sidebar, 9:16 social-safe (TikTok/Reels safe zones), raw no-re-encode batch export. Its telemetry is entirely from Tesla's embedded SEI — it has no external data source. Sentry-Six/Sentry Studio (Electron, MIT, free) was first-to-market with a SEI telemetry dashboard overlay and adds GPU export (NVENC/AMD/QSV/Apple Silicon), blur zones, GPS minimap, 13 languages; its ecosystem includes a Raspberry-Pi smart USB drive with auto-archive and an iOS companion. ExportDash (MIT, Next.js, 126 stars) and NateMccomb/TeslaCamViewer (MIT, browser, AI plate-blur via WASM YOLOv11n/ESRGAN) are the strongest open-source browser references; DeaglePC TDashcamStudio (AGPL, Tauri, EN/CN) pioneered the speed-curve-in-scrubber idea. ehendrix23/tesla_dashcam (Python CLI, 734 stars, last stable v0.1.21 ~Dec 2023) remains the layout-richest batch composer (FULLSCREEN/MOSAIC/PERSPECTIVE/CROSS/DIAMOND/HORIZONTAL, per-camera scale/position, motion-only fast-forward, folder-watch monitor mode) but has no telemetry. Commercial generic option: Telemetry Overlay ($199, goprotelemetryextractor.com) explicitly supports TeslaCam SEI AND TeslaMate CSV exported via Grafana, with 40+ gauges and transparent-overlay export — it is the only existing tool that combines both sources, but requires manual CSV export and manual time alignment. time4tea/gopro-dashboard-overlay is the open-source analog (GPX/FIT input, XML layouts). Older/simpler viewers (Blazor TeslaCamPlayer, teslacam-browser CC0 238 stars, Microsoft Store TeslaCam, TCam UWP, Mac Sentry Viewer, web players teslacam.xyz/tesclip.com/sentrycam.appspot.com) do sync playback only, no telemetry, mostly stale. Tesla's own in-car viewer + mobile app now show the telemetry overlay too, and downloaded app clips retain SEI.

GAP ANALYSIS FOR OHMYTESLA: no tool today joins SEI frame data with a longitudinal database. SEI gives 30-36Hz precision but only while driving and only post-2025.44.25; TeslaMate Postgres (positions table ~1Hz: speed, power kW, SOC, elevation, lat/lon, battery_heater, outside_temp; drives, charges, geofences tables) covers every car since 2019 and adds SOC/power/elevation/temps that SEI lacks. Clip filename wall-clock + SEI GPS can be cross-correlated against TeslaMate positions to auto-align clocks. That fusion — plus drive-centric browsing (pick a drive in TeslaMate, see its footage) — is unoccupied territory.

feature_ideas: TeslaMate-fused overlay (the moat): time-match video to TeslaMate Postgres and overlay data NO SEI-based tool can show — battery SOC, power/regen kW bar, elevation profile, inside/outside temperature, odometer, remaining range, charger events. SEI gives speed/steering/pedals/GPS at 30-36Hz; TeslaMate fills everything else at ~1Hz. Render SEI-driven gauges at frame rate, TeslaMate-driven gauges interpolated.

Backfill telemetry for pre-SEI footage: clips recorded before firmware 2025.44.25 (and many parked Sentry clips) have zero embedded telemetry — derive speed/GPS/power overlays purely from TeslaMate positions matched by clip filename timestamp. No existing tool can do this; it instantly serves years-old footage.

Drive-centric browsing instead of folder-centric: pick a drive from TeslaMate's drives table and see its footage stitched as one continuous timeline with the route map; conversely, clicking any point on a TeslaMate drive map jumps the video there. All current tools start from the USB folder tree.

Clock-drift auto-correction: cross-correlate SEI lat/lon (or speed curve) against TeslaMate positions to compute the exact offset between car-file timestamps and TeslaMate wall clock, instead of trusting filenames (Telemetry Overlay makes users align by hand).

Sentry event enrichment: join SentryClips event.json (reason, est_lat/est_lon, timestamp) with TeslaMate geofences to auto-tag events ('Sentry @ Home', 'Sentry @ Office'), filter by location, and show a sentry-events heat map.

Timeline intelligence bands (steal from bt1142msstate + DeaglePC): speed curve rendered in the scrubber background, yellow bands for manual driving vs FSD/Autosteer, markers for hard braking (linear_acceleration threshold), honks, disengagements; per-clip FSD% and disengagement-count indexing stored in Postgres.

Layout parity + one better: 2x2/6-grid, picture-in-picture, cockpit, sidebar, fullscreen-with-thumbnail-cycling, 9:16 social-safe vertical (RedDash), plus a drag-and-drop custom layout editor (NateMccomb) with per-camera crop/scale — and save layouts as shareable presets.

Map overlay in the EXPORT, not just the viewer: burned-in minimap with route trace colored by autopilot state (blue FSD / gray manual, like Sentry Studio's viewer) — most tools only show the map live, not in exported video.

Export pipeline choices: server-side ffmpeg with NVENC/QSV/VideoToolbox (tesla_dashcam-class quality tiers, x264/x265) for long merges, plus instant client-side WebCodecs+mp4-muxer export for short clips; also transparent-overlay-only export for pro editors (Telemetry Overlay feature).

Privacy toolkit: blur zones, AI license-plate/face blurring via local WASM models (YOLOv11n as in NateMccomb), and a privacy export mode stripping GPS/timestamps — table stakes for sharing sentry footage publicly.

Handle 2026.20 encryption explicitly: detect encrypted clips, guide users to Controls > Safety > Encrypt Dashcam Recordings, and/or implement Tesla-account-key local decryption like ExportDash and dashcam.tesla.com — tools that ignore this are already breaking.

Robustness features users complain about elsewhere: tolerate missing/corrupt camera angles (Rene-Sackers), moov-at-end files, mixed H.264/H.265 archives, MCU1 3-camera sets; motion-only fast-forward (tesla_dashcam) for hours of parked Sentry footage.

Data exports: telemetry CSV/GPX per clip or per drive (several tools), and 'evidence package' export: composed video + raw clips + event.json + telemetry CSV + map snapshot in one ZIP for insurance claims.

Auto-ingest: watch mode that indexes a mounted TeslaCam drive (or TeslaUSB/Sentry-USB network share) into Postgres on plug-in — folder scan, event.json parse, one-time SEI extraction into tables so timeline queries and analytics are instant on revisit.
recommendations: Parse SEI with Tesla's official schema: vendor github.com/teslamotors/dashcam's dashcam.proto and follow dashcam-mp4.js / sei_extractor.py for NAL extraction; use protobufjs client-side (ExportDash/teslanav-viewer precedent) or Python server-side. frame_seq_no gives exact per-frame ordering; vehicle_speed_mps is m/s (convert), autopilot_state distinguishes NONE/TACC/AUTOSTEER/SELF_DRIVING.

Ingest-once architecture: since OhmyTesla already runs Postgres, add tables (clips, clip_frames_telemetry or downsampled 1Hz clip_telemetry, events) and extract SEI at import time rather than on every playback — enables SQL joins against TeslaMate drives/positions/geofences and fast analytics (FSD%, disengagements, hard-braking search).

Codec strategy is the #1 web-viewer pitfall: HW3 pre-2023 clips are H.264 (plays everywhere), everything since is HEVC. Chrome/Edge only decode HEVC with platform hardware support; Chromium-in-Electron often can't. Probe codec per file (ffprobe/mp4box), play natively when possible, and fall back to on-the-fly server ffmpeg transcode or WASM decode. Note moov atom at file end — either fast-start remux on ingest or serve whole files.

Time model: treat clip filename (YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS local time) as coarse start, refine with SEI GPS-vs-TeslaMate-positions cross-correlation; interpolate TeslaMate 1Hz data (positions: speed, power, SOC, elevation) with monotonic interpolation onto video PTS; beware TeslaMate timestamps are UTC while clip filenames are car-local time.

Composition engine: for burned exports use ffmpeg filtergraphs (xstack/overlay/drawtext) with hwaccel selection per platform (NVENC, QSV/VAAPI, VideoToolbox) exactly as tesla_dashcam does — its layout definitions (MOSAIC/CROSS/DIAMOND/etc.) are a proven taxonomy to copy; render telemetry gauges to a transparent frame sequence or Canvas-captured overlay track composited over the camera grid.
For instant in-browser clip export use WebCodecs + mp4-muxer (ExportDash/teslanav-viewer stack); keep server ffmpeg for multi-minute merges and 6-camera 2896x1876 loads where browser memory dies.

Maps: MapLibre GL JS or Leaflet with OSM tiles; draw route from TeslaMate positions (works even without SEI), color segments by autopilot_state when SEI present; for exported video pre-render map tiles server-side (gopro-dashboard-overlay approach) to avoid live-tile licensing/perf issues.

License hygiene: MIT references you may read/borrow from: ExportDash, Sentry-Six, NateMccomb TeslaCamViewer, teslanav-viewer; AGPL-3.0 (DeaglePC) and source-available (bt1142msstate) — ideas only, no code; tesla_dashcam is a CLI you could even shell out to for batch composition.

Plan for encryption (2026.20+ default-on): detect .mp4 files that fail to parse as clear MP4, surface a clear UX explaining the Controls > Safety toggle, and investigate the dashcam.tesla.com local-decryption flow (account-tied key) that ExportDash reverse-implemented — otherwise every new-firmware user's first experience is 'broken files'.

Per-camera geometry differs on HW4 (front 2896x1876 vs others 1448x938, HW3 all 1280x960, fps 36 vs ~30/24): never hardcode dimensions; probe each stream and normalize via scale filters; support 4-, 6-, and 7-camera (Cybertruck rear-backup) sets and gracefully degrade on missing angles.

sentry.summary: SENTRY EVENT DETECTION — GROUND TRUTH. The ONLY near-real-time source of sentry events for third parties is Tesla Fleet Telemetry. Its protobuf (teslamotors/fleet-telemetry protos/vehicle_data.proto, 874 stars) defines field SentryMode (field 65) with enum SentryModeState: Unknown/Off/Idle/Armed/Aware/Panic/Quiet. "Aware" = sentry detected motion/proximity (the event all commercial apps alert on); "Panic" = alarm. Related fields: CenterDisplay (DisplayStateLock state = someone touched a locked car, usable for break-in alerts even with sentry OFF), ChargePortLatch (used to suppress cable-plug false positives), Locked, GuestModeEnabled. Delivery semantics (developer.tesla.com): a field is sent only when interval_seconds has elapsed AND the value changed; firmware 2024.44.32+ adds minimum_delta and resend_interval_seconds. Telemetry requires: Tesla developer/partner app registration, hosted public key, VIRTUAL KEY paired to vehicle (exception: pre-2021 Model S/X on firmware 2025.20+), firmware 2023.20.6+, and a publicly reachable mTLS fleet-telemetry server (FQDN + CA cert); dispatchers: Kafka, Kinesis, Pub/Sub, ZMQ, MQTT, Redis, logger. No Premium Connectivity needed. BY CONTRAST: (a) Fleet API vehicle_data only exposes vehicle_state.sentry_mode (boolean on/off), sentry_mode_available, and center_display_state (7 = sentry showing) — NO event/Aware/alarm field exists (confirmed by TeslaMate maintainers in teslamate discussion #3292: "There is no API endpoint today that delivers this value"), so polling can never see sentry events, only arming state; (b) vehicle_data polling is also cost-prohibitive on Fleet API: $0.002/request (2 credits) → 1-min polling ≈ $86/mo vs $10/mo free credit; streaming signals cost $0.0001/signal (a SentryMode-only on-change stream costs pennies); commands $0.001, wake $0.02 (Teslemetry pay-per-use blog); (c) the legacy Owner API WebSocket stream (wss://streaming.vn.teslamotors.com, still used by TeslaMate 4.1.0-dev) carries only driving fields: speed, odometer, soc, elevation, est_heading, est_lat, est_lng, power, shift_state, range, est_range, heading — no sentry/alarm; (d) TeslaMate MQTT publishes teslamate/cars/$car_id/sentry_mode (boolean) and center_display_state at polling cadence (POLLING_ONLINE_INTERVAL=60s idle, default 15s, driving 2.5s; sentry_mode:true blocks suspend, vehicle.ex:1839) — no alarm/event topic exists; (e) Tesla's own app pushes only "Security Alerts" (alarm trigger, door/trunk opened, impact while away) and NEVER routine sentry proximity/motion events — this gap is the entire market for these apps. SENTRYPRO (sentrypro.app, iOS+Android, "Approved Tesla Fleet API developer"): detects events via Fleet API/Fleet Telemetry ("receives events from Tesla's Fleet API when Sentry Mode records activity"); virtual key required, MCU2 S/X needs 2025.20+, MCU1 unsupported — signature matches Fleet Telemetry SentryMode=Aware detection. Pricing $5.99/mo, $49.99/yr, $133.99 lifetime, 7-day trial, all vehicles on one sub. Features: push "within seconds", iOS Critical Alerts (Auto = escalate after 90s of continued activity, or Always), 15-second continuous-event dedup, auto-honk/flash/boombox deterrents, backend-side sentry scheduling (works with phone off), activity feed, battery data (sentry ≈150W on 2024.38+, ~3.6 kWh/24h = 4-8% pack/day). Admits 2+ min delays in poor LTE and cannot distinguish automatic vs event-driven activations. SENTRYALERT (sentryalert.app): explicitly "streams Sentry Mode events in real time via Tesla Fleet Telemetry", auto telemetry setup, push per event, remote honk/flash, 5 vehicles/account, 30-day filtered event history, 7-day trial then monthly/annual sub. SENTRY MODDER: subscription iOS/Android app, all-events notifications, honk/flash/fart auto-responses, time/location-based sentry scheduling, history. TESSIE: $12.99/mo per vehicle ($299.99 lifetime); "Sentry Tracking" auto-records all sentry events, Movement + Alarm push alerts require enabling "Direct Telemetry" (Tessie's Fleet Telemetry); claims zero battery impact; passive (no deterrent automation). TESLAFI: no sentry event alerts — only emails when its scheduler toggles sentry. SENTRYGUARD (github.com/abarghoud/SentryGuard, AGPL-3.0, 209 stars, pushed 2026-08-04, actively developed): the key open-source reference. Stack: NestJS/TypeORM/Postgres/Telegraf backend, Next.js 15 frontend, Expo mobile, Docker Compose self-hosting (SELF_HOSTING.md) including its own fleet-telemetry ingest (port 8443) and tesla-vehicle-command proxy. Verified source facts: patches fleet_telemetry_config with {SentryMode:{interval_seconds:30}} (env-tunable); fires alert when SentryModeState == Aware; break-in detection with sentry OFF via CenterDisplay == DisplayStateLock with delayed verification plus ChargePortLatch time-correlation to suppress charge-cable false alarms; Telegram delivery with deep-linked chat setup, inline keyboards (mute, honk/boombox "offensive response" per vehicle); measures end-to-end latency via correlationId, flags processing >1s. Free hosted tier run non-profit (may move to ~$0.50/user). MYTESLAMATE (myteslamate.com): Fleet API proxy + telemetry for self-hosted TeslaMate (free tier; pay-as-you-go 500 credits/€1; 1 credit = 300 API calls, 20 = wake); re-emulates the old Owner streaming WebSocket from Fleet Telemetry so stock TeslaMate keeps working (TESLA_API_HOST/TESLA_WSS_HOST env vars); offers Telegram sentry/break-in alerts (SentryGuard-based), door-handle alerts with sentry off, auto-honk, charge-cable false-alarm suppression; can expose secure MQTT + TeslaMateAPI. TESLEMETRY: $2.50/mo base + $2.50/vehicle data sub (32 cached vehicle_data calls/day) + command credit packs, aimed at Home Assistant. TESLAUSB (marcone/teslausb, MIT, 2338 stars): Pi USB-gadget archiver — notifies only after clips sync on home WiFi, not real-time. TESLAMATE itself (AGPL, 8805 stars): no notification engine; community wires MQTT → Node-RED/Home Assistant → Telegram/email (website/docs/integrations/Node-RED.md ships a Telegram notification flow). NOTIFICATION CHANNELS: ntfy (binwiederhier/ntfy, Apache-2.0, 33k stars): HTTP PUT/POST to a topic, no account needed on ntfy.sh, self-hostable; iOS caveat — self-hosted instances need upstream-base-url relay via ntfy.sh for APNS-instant delivery, else delays of 20 min-hours. Gotify (15.6k stars): self-hosted WebSocket push, official Android client only — no official iOS app. Pushover: proprietary, $5 one-time per platform after 30-day trial, 10k msgs/mo, very reliable APNS/FCM. Telegram bot: free, instant, cross-platform, supports actionable inline buttons (proven by SentryGuard/MyTeslaMate). Discord webhook: free single POST, push via Discord app. SMTP: universal fallback, not push-latency-reliable. Web Push: free, self-generated VAPID keys, no vendor account; works on iOS 16.4+ ONLY when the PWA is added to Home Screen (standalone mode) and permission is requested from a direct user tap; fine on Android/desktop browsers. Apprise (caronc/apprise, BSD-2-Clause, 17k stars): Python lib + API container normalizing 100+ services behind one URL syntax — ideal extensibility layer.

feature_ideas: Alert on Fleet Telemetry SentryMode Armed→Aware transition (the industry-standard event signal), with Panic treated as a critical alarm tier — exactly what SentryPro/SentryAlert/Tessie/SentryGuard all do

Continuous-event deduplication: collapse Aware states recurring without a 15s pause into one incident (SentryPro), with escalation to critical/DND-override if activity persists 90s (SentryPro Critical Alerts Auto mode)

Per-incident end-to-end latency measurement (event timestamp vs delivery) surfaced as a health metric (SentryGuard correlationId pattern)
Multi-vehicle support under one account/config (SentryPro all-cars-one-sub vs Tessie per-car billing is a marketing point)
False-positive suppression when owner is present: skip alerts if is_user_present/phone-key nearby or car unlocked by owner
Publish sentry events to TeslaMate-style MQTT topics (e.g. teslamate/cars/$car_id/sentry_event) so Home Assistant/Node-RED users can automate — no existing product does this
Optional home-WiFi TeslaCam clip sync integration (teslausb) to attach actual video to incident records after the car returns home
recommendations: Event source: use Fleet Telemetry, not polling. vehicle_data has no sentry-event field (only sentry_mode bool + center_display_state=7), so polling is architecturally blind to events, adds up to 60s lag through TeslaMate's online interval, and costs $0.002/request on Fleet API (~$86/mo at 1-min cadence) vs $0.0001/signal for on-change streaming that fits inside Tesla's $10/mo free credit.

Concrete telemetry config: fleet_telemetry_config with fields {SentryMode:{interval_seconds:1..30}, CenterDisplay:{interval_seconds:30}, ChargePortLatch:{interval_seconds:30}} — values transmit only on change, so a 1s interval on SentryMode is nearly free and gives 1-5s end-to-end latency on good LTE (worst case minutes in poor coverage; both SentryPro and SentryGuard document this).

Three deployment tiers for a self-hosted TeslaMate-based web app: (1) EASY — point the car's telemetry at MyTeslaMate (free tier) and consume their MQTT/streaming re-emission next to the existing TeslaMate integration; (2) FULL CONTROL — self-host teslamotors/fleet-telemetry (Go) with the MQTT dispatcher into the same broker TeslaMate already uses; requires Tesla developer app registration, hosted public key, FQDN + CA-signed TLS + mTLS, and a virtual key on the vehicle; (3) REUSE — SentryGuard is AGPL-3.0 (same license as TeslaMate) and its NestJS handlers (Aware detection, DisplayStateLock break-in logic, ChargePortLatch debounce) can be embedded or run as a sidecar docker-compose service.

Detection state machine: alert on Armed/Idle/Quiet→Aware; critical-alert on →Panic; debounce consecutive Aware within 15s into one incident; escalate if activity persists 90s; suppress when is_user_present or a charge-latch event correlates within the verification window; record every transition with timestamps for the incident timeline.

Battery/API cost truth for docs: sentry mode itself keeps the car awake (~150W on fw 2024.38+, 4-8% pack/day) — telemetry streaming adds nothing measurable, and polling while sentry is armed also doesn't add battery drain (car already awake, TeslaMate never suspends with sentry on) — polling's real costs are blindness to events, latency, and Fleet API fees.

Default notification channel set for a self-hosted web app: (1) Telegram bot as the flagship default — free, instant on iOS+Android, supports actionable inline buttons (honk/mute), proven by SentryGuard/MyTeslaMate; (2) Web Push for the app's own PWA — free, self-generated VAPID, no third-party account, but document iOS 16.4+ requirements (must be installed to Home Screen, permission requested from a user tap); (3) ntfy for the self-hosted crowd — no account needed, HTTP POST, but self-hosted servers need upstream-base-url=ntfy.sh relay for instant iOS delivery; (4) SMTP email as universal fallback. Offer Pushover ($5 one-time, most reliable mobile push) and Discord webhook as cheap options, and integrate Apprise (BSD-2, 100+ services, single-URL config) as the extensibility layer instead of hand-writing more integrations. Avoid Gotify as a default: no official iOS client.

Also publish each sentry incident to MQTT (TeslaMate-topic style) so Home Assistant/Node-RED users can build their own automations — this matches the existing TeslaMate integration culture (the official docs' Node-RED Telegram flow) and costs nothing.

Latency budget to advertise honestly: car→Tesla→your telemetry endpoint typically 1-3s, total push under 5s on good LTE; state clearly (as SentryPro does) that poor cellular coverage can delay alerts by minutes and that MCU1 cars are unsupported and MCU2 S/X need fw 2025.20+ with virtual-key exemption rules for pre-2021 S/X.

analytics.summary:
Market survey of Tesla data/analytics companions (Aug 2026), for a grand-unification open-source app.

COMMERCIAL LOGGERS. TeslaFi (web-only, ~$5/mo): polls Owner API; core = timeline of drive/charge/sleep/idle sessions, per-drive maps+elevation+weather, drive tagging/categories, calendar view, charge logs by location with cost (TOU), temperature-vs-efficiency report, fleet software-update tracker, battery degradation report (rated range extrapolated to 100%, filters: exclude incomplete charges / charges <80%) with fleet comparison matched by odometer ±999 and temperature ±99F, command scheduling (any command at times), Alexa skill, leaderboards, gas-savings cost analysis, TeslaFi API tokens + raw CSV export. Its signature complexity is sleep management: "time to try sleeping" (pause polling ~15 min), deep-sleep time windows, sleep-readiness heuristics, raw polling feed page — all workarounds for polling keeping the car awake. Tessie (iOS/Android/web/Watch/WearOS, ~$5/mo, owned by MWM, 500k+ drivers, 2.6B+ mi): streaming/Fleet-Telemetry based (no sleep problem); trips + drive analytics (avg/peak speed), charging + phantom-drain tracking, Lock Screen Live Activity while charging, sleep score, Low Power Mode, Keep Accessory Power, FSD usage tracking, internet connectivity monitoring, charge projections, "since last charge" views, Profiler (real-time OBD-level diagnostics without a dongle), custom themes, importers from TezLab/TeslaFi/Teslascope/TeslaMate. Battery health: BMS-derived capacity recorded after every charge >5 kWh; health = current range ÷ original range, original capacity seeded from fleet average for the same config (user-overridable); shows health %, cycles (full-charge equivalents), graphs of max range/capacity/cycles/lifetime energy; continuous, unlike Tesla's test. Alerts (very complete list): firmware/hardware/service alerts, software update, weather warning (precipitation with window/door/trunk open), unlocked doors, climate safety (Dog Mode temp exceeded), Sentry movement + Sentry alarm, drive start/end, speed threshold, location arrival/departure (geofence), charge start/end, reduced/no charger power, low battery, not plugged in, low tire pressure, maintenance reminders (tire rotation, brake fluid, cabin filter, HEPA, A/C desiccant). Automations: cloud-run if-this-then-that; triggers = arrival/departure/plugged-in/Sentry movement/Sentry alarm (optionally at a place) + schedules; actions = climate, charge start/stop, charge limit, amps, charge port, Sentry, etc. Integrations: Alexa, HomeKit, Home Assistant (official HA integration), Mac/PC web control. Developer API (api.tessie.com): own REST API (state, battery, drives, idles, paths, historical states, tire pressure, commands) PLUS transparent pass-through to Tesla Fleet API with automatic NA/EU/CN region routing and automatic Vehicle Command Protocol signing — widely used as an easier Fleet API. Teslascope (web+iOS; free / Plus $3.99 / Pro $6.99 per vehicle/mo): drives on maps + calendar, charging analytics, battery health from Fleet Telemetry (usable capacity, health %, equivalent cycles), cost calc (TOU + per-location kWh rates), Supercharger cost sync + invoice downloads (Pro), automations/vehicle schedules (time/trigger/location), speed & zone-departure alerts, free "Restful Sleep Mode", fleet-public software-update tracking (installs-over-time graphs, release notes archive), leaderboards incl. AI4 self-driving miles + usage %, Groups/communities, public vehicle profiles, driver management + invite links, passkeys/2FA/AES-256, Developer OAuth + scoped personal access tokens. Stats app (iOS one-time purchase, maadotaa.com): battery health graph (100% rated range vs odometer) + estimated capacity + fleet comparison per model, phantom drain by day/week/month/location, efficiency trends vs other users, charging schedule/stop-at-time for TOU, charge reminders, battery warm-up, climate schedules, auto-lock-if-left-unlocked, door/trunk/frunk/unlocked notifications, dashcam/Sentry video viewing, widgets, Siri Shortcuts, Watch app, multi-vehicle, spreadsheet export, firmware distribution stats. TezLab (iOS/Android, freemium, also Rivian): battery range performance trend (extrapolated full-charge range), charge details (kW, kWh, duration, est. CO2 kg), phantom drain, efficiency %, leaderboards, achievement badges, CO2 impact + tree planting. tesla-info.com has REBRANDED to ev-inventory.com: inventory search (new/used/CPO) with email+push alerts, depreciation/market valuation, production rate by VIN, VIN/option-code/data decoders, token generator, manual battery-capacity calculation guide + API-based fleet battery benchmark, BMS calibration guidance, buyers guides, release-notes archive. Watch ecosystem: official Tesla Watch app (complications = SoC/energy; controls incl. trunk/charge port/lights/horn); Watchla = watch-as-BLE-key, offline BLE control, complications.

CAN/OBD LAYER. Scan My Tesla (Android; "scan my t3sla" iOS): connects to CAN via model-specific wiring harness (Tesla's OBD2 port carries only 12V+VIN); adapters = OBDLink MX+ (BT) and CANserver (WiFi). Hundreds of live signals: nominal full pack kWh, usable full pack, capacity estimates, battery lifetime stats (total charge/discharge kWh, AC vs DC totals), pack voltage/current/power, per-brick cell voltage map, min/max cell temps, coolant temps, drive unit torque/HP/RPM/temps, power/regen limits, HVAC internals, 12V system, 0-60/0-100 timers, trip recording incl. charging, CAN dump export (SavvyCAN). Its degradation feature ('Full pack when new' vs 'Nominal full pack', Model 3/Y only) was REMOVED as incorrect (counted factory "initial settling"). CAN-only data vs API: cell-level voltages/temps/imbalance, BMS nominal/usable pack energy directly, lifetime energy counters, torque/power limits — none exposed by Fleet API (though Fleet Telemetry now exposes some pack signals used by Teslascope/Tessie for health). ABRP (free + Premium $50/yr): 1000+ data-driven consumption models (speed/elevation/weather/HVAC/battery-temp aware), adaptive consumption profiles calibrated from real driving, live vehicle data (Tesla account link for SoC/position; OBD dongle; bridges from Tessie/TeslaFi/TeslaMate-MQTT (teslamate-abrp)/OVMS), auto re-planning while driving, live charger availability + amenity/photo/pricing data, live traffic, speed cameras, CarPlay/Android Auto/Android Automotive, watch app, saved/shared plans, drive & charge history; claims 3-5% SoC prediction accuracy with live telemetry.

BATTERY-HEALTH METHODOLOGIES (the key differentiator): (1) Range-based (TeslaFi/Stats/TezLab): rated range extrapolated to 100% trended vs odometer/time; sensitive to BMS estimate drift. (2) Tessie: same range ratio but anchored to fleet-average new capacity per config, sampled from BMS after each >5kWh charge. (3) TeslaMate core battery-health dashboard (verified in local repo <repo>/teslamate/grafana/dashboards/battery-health.json): derived_efficiency = charge_energy_added / (end_rated_range_km − start_rated_range_km) using the most common value over charges >10 min ending ≤95%; capacity kWh = rated_range_km × efficiency / usable_battery_level; "current capacity" = avg of last 100 qualifying charge points; "max capacity" = historical max; health % = current/max (with $custom_kwh_new override); panels: Battery Capacity (trend), Capacity by Mileage, Estimated Degradation, Ranges, Current Stored Energy, AC/DC energy used, charging/drive stats. (4) Fleet-Telemetry BMS signals (Teslascope, Tessie Profiler) — closest to ground truth without hardware. (5) CAN (SMT): direct BMS nominal full pack. (6) Tesla official: in-app pass/fail check (Service > Battery & Charging > Range; newer app versions incl. China show an actual %), and Service Mode HV "Health Test": scripted discharge then charge to 100%, needs 12-48h plugged in, outputs capacity-retention %; Tesla discourages frequent use. recommendations: Build ingestion on Tesla Fleet Telemetry (push/streaming) as primary, with Owner-API polling only as legacy fallback — this eliminates the entire TeslaFi-style sleep-management problem class and gives BMS-grade signals that Teslascope/Tessie already use for battery health; keep a TeslaMate-style polling adapter for older firmware.

Implement battery health as a multi-estimator pipeline, not one number: (a) TeslaMate derived-efficiency estimator (charge_energy_added / rated-range delta, filtered charges >10min end<=95%, rolling avg of last ~100 points vs historical max — SQL already in grafana/dashboards/battery-health.json in the local repo), (b) range-ratio estimator, (c) Fleet Telemetry BMS pack-energy signals when available, (d) optional Scan-My-Tesla/CAN import for ground truth. Show confidence bands and let users pin 'capacity when new' — SMT removed its degradation number because factory settling made single-source numbers wrong; learn from that.

Ship an alerts + automations engine early (triggers: geofence, plugged-in, SOC, time, Sentry; actions: full command set). This is the single biggest functional gap between TeslaMate and Tessie/Teslascope and the top reason users pay subscriptions.

Expose three integration surfaces from day one: MQTT (retain TeslaMate compatibility for Home Assistant/ABRP bridges), a REST API with PAT/OAuth scopes, and a telemetry-export format consumable by dashcam viewers (Sentry Clip Viewer already integrates TeslaMate/Tessie data) — being the best data hub is cheaper than building every UI.

Write importers for TeslaFi CSV, Tessie export, TezLab and Teslascope archives (Tessie proves import is a growth lever), and an exporter so users never feel locked in — key open-source differentiator.

Do not rebuild route planning; integrate with ABRP via the established teslamate-abrp MQTT bridge pattern, but keep a local consumption model (Wh/km vs speed/temp/elevation from logged drives) for in-app range projection.

Fleet comparison features (degradation percentile matched by model/pack/odometer/climate, firmware rollout tracking) require aggregated multi-user data: design an opt-in anonymized telemetry pool now (self-hosters push summary stats to a community service), since this is the one feature class pure self-hosting cannot deliver.

Treat cost tracking as first-class schema: per-geofence tariffs, TOU windows, tiered rates, Supercharger invoice ingestion (Teslascope does invoice sync via Tesla account), and business/personal drive tagging for tax-ready mileage export.

For China support, plan for the separate China Fleet API region, data-residency constraints, and WeChat mini-program delivery; feature parity references are 小特 (community + charging map + ground-lock unlock) and offline BLE key (小特钥匙).

Command execution must implement Tesla Vehicle Command Protocol signing (Tessie monetizes just this); consider vendoring Tesla's official vehicle-command Go proxy or an Elixir equivalent rather than reimplementing.

Mobile/watch presence matters: minimum viable = PWA + Lock Screen Live Activity substitute, home-screen widgets, and a Watch complication for SOC; Stats app shows deep OS integration (Siri Shortcuts, widgets) drives one-time-purchase loyalty.

Keep Grafana as the power-user layer but put a curated first-party UI in front of the top 6 views (overview, drive detail, charge detail, battery health, costs, software updates) — Grafana UX is the most cited TeslaMate adoption barrier vs Tessie.

tminternals.summary: TeslaMate (repo at <repo>/teslamate, VERSION 4.1.0-dev) is an Elixir/Phoenix 1.7 + LiveView app that logs one or more Tesla vehicles by combining Owner-API polling (state-dependent intervals, 2.5s while driving) with the ~1 Hz Owner streaming WebSocket, persists everything to Postgres in metric units (km/h, kW, km, °C, bar, microsecond timestamps), republishes a live car summary to MQTT under teslamate/cars/$car_id/..., and ships 23 provisioned Grafana dashboards that read the Postgres DB directly. Companion services are expected to integrate via MQTT (live state) and direct Postgres reads (history); the app itself exposes almost no HTTP API (only PUT /api/car/:id/logging/{resume,suspend}, GET /drive/:id/gpx, GET /health_check). The web UI is translated to Simplified and Traditional Chinese. For dashcam overlay: during a streaming drive the positions table gets ~1 row/second containing date (ms precision), lat/lon, speed (int km/h), power (int kW), battery_level, elevation (int m), odometer (km) — but no heading column; heading exists only on the live MQTT topic or must be derived from consecutive coordinates.
facts: STACK: mix.exs requires Elixir ~> 1.17; key deps: phoenix ~> 1.7.0, phoenix_live_view ~> 1.2.8, ecto_sql ~> 3.0, postgrex, tortoise311 ~> 0.12 (MQTT client), websockex ~> 0.5 (Tesla streaming), tesla ~> 1.14 + finch (HTTP), srtm ~> 0.8 (elevation fallback), cloak_ecto ~> 1.3 (token encryption), gen_state_machine (vehicle FSM). App version comes from the VERSION file: currently '4.1.0-dev'.

DOCKER: Dockerfile builds with elixir:1.19.5-otp-28 + Node 22 (esbuild/sass asset build via 'mix assets.deploy' -> assets/scripts/build.js), releases with 'mix release', and runs on debian:trixie-slim as user nonroot with tini; EXPOSE 4000. entrypoint.sh waits for Postgres via nc, then runs 'bin/teslamate eval TeslaMate.Release.migrate' before starting — migrations are applied automatically at container start.

ASSET PIPELINE: assets/package.json — esbuild + esbuild-sass-plugin, Bulma CSS, leaflet 1.9 + @geoman-io/leaflet-geoman-free + leaflet-control-geocoder (geofence map editor), phoenix/phoenix_html/phoenix_live_view JS from deps. No webpack.

OFFICIAL docker-compose (website/docs/installation/docker.md): 4 services — teslamate/teslamate:latest (port 4000, env ENCRYPTION_KEY, DATABASE_USER/PASS/NAME/HOST, MQTT_HOST, volume ./import:/opt/app/import), postgres:18-trixie, teslamate/grafana:latest (port 3000, DATABASE_* env), eclipse-mosquitto:2 (no-auth config). Named volumes teslamate-db, teslamate-grafana-data, mosquitto-conf/data.

MQTT TOPIC PATTERN (lib/teslamate/mqtt/pubsub/vehicle_subscriber.ex): topics are teslamate/[$MQTT_NAMESPACE/]cars/$car_id/<key> where car_id is the internal Postgres cars.id (usually starts at 1). Published with QoS 1, retain: true for everything except 'healthy' (never retained; old retained healthy messages are actively cleared). Values are published only when they change; keys in @publish_if_nil (charge_energy_added, charger_actual_current, charger_phases, charger_power, charger_voltage, scheduled_charging_start_time, time_to_full_charge, shift_state, geofence, trim_badging) are also published when nil (empty payload).

GRAFANA: teslamate/grafana image = grafana/grafana:13.1.1 (grafana/Dockerfile) with provisioning: grafana/datasource.yml defines a Postgres datasource named 'TeslaMate' pointing straight at the TeslaMate DB (DATABASE_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/NAME env), grafana/dashboards.yml provisions three folders — TeslaMate (/dashboards), Internal (/dashboards_internal), Reports (/dashboards_reports); home dashboard = internal/home.json. Dashboard titles (grafana/dashboards/*.json): Battery Health, Charge Level, Charges, Charging Stats, Database Information, Drive Stats, Drives, Efficiency, Locations, Mileage, Overview, Projected Range, States, Statistics, Timeline, Trip, Updates, Vampire Drain, Visited; internal/: Charge Details, Drive Details, Home; reports/: Drives - Dutch tax.

WEB UI (lib/teslamate_web/router.ex): GET / renders CarLive.Index (live car tiles with summary/state); LiveViews: /sign_in (token-based Tesla login), /settings (per-car: data collection enable, sleep-mode suspend timings, 'vehicle must be locked' requirement, free supercharging, Streaming API toggle, LFP battery; global: units, preferred range, language for OSM geocoding, theme mode, base/grafana URL, sign out), /geo-fences + /geo-fences/new + /geo-fences/:id/edit (Leaflet map editor, phx-hook='Map', draggable radius, per_kwh/per_minute cost, session fee, retroactive charge-cost recalculation), /charge-cost/:id (edit cost of one charging session), /import (TeslaFi CSV import — files named TeslaFi<M><YYYY>.csv from IMPORT_DIR). GET /drive/:id/gpx exports a drive as GPX (lib/teslamate_web/controllers/drive_controller.ex).

HTTP/JSON API surface (the ONLY programmatic HTTP endpoints, lib/teslamate_web/router.ex + car_controller.ex + health_check.ex): PUT /api/car/:id/logging/resume, PUT /api/car/:id/logging/suspend (no auth), GET /health_check (200 empty, plugged in endpoint.ex), GET /drive/:id/gpx. There is no general REST/JSON data API — that role is filled by the community TeslaMateApi project (Golang, reads Postgres + MQTT), listed in website/docs/projects.md.

TESLA AUTH (lib/tesla_api/auth.ex, auth/refresh.ex, lib/teslamate/api.ex): sign-in is by pasting Tesla access+refresh tokens (SignInLive); TeslaMate never handles Tesla password login anymore. Tokens are stored AES-encrypted (TeslaMate.Vault, ENCRYPTION_KEY) in private.tokens. Access token auto-refresh is scheduled at 75% of expires_in via POST {issuer}/token with grant_type=refresh_token, scope 'openid email offline_access', client_id from TESLA_AUTH_CLIENT_ID (default 'ownerapi'). Region detection from token prefix/JWT iss: .cn -> Chinese endpoints.

TESLA DATA PLANE 2026 (lib/tesla_api/vehicle.ex, stream.ex; website/docs/configuration/api.md): default remains the unofficial Owner API — GET /api/1/products, GET /api/1/vehicles/:id, GET /api/1/vehicles/:id/vehicle_data?endpoints=charge_state;climate_state;closures_state;drive_state;gui_settings;location_data;vehicle_config;vehicle_state;vehicle_data_combo on https://owner-api.teslamotors.com (China: https://owner-api.vn.cloud.tesla.cn) — plus the Owner streaming WebSocket wss://streaming.vn.teslamotors.com/streaming/ (China: wss://streaming.vn.cloud.tesla.cn) subscribing columns speed,odometer,soc,elevation,est_heading,est_lat,est_lng,power,shift_state,range,est_range,heading via msg data:subscribe_oauth. Fleet API / Fleet Telemetry are supported ONLY by env override: TESLA_API_HOST, TESLA_AUTH_HOST, TESLA_AUTH_PATH, TESLA_AUTH_CLIENT_ID, TESLA_WSS_HOST, TESLA_WSS_USE_VIN, and TOKEN (fleet-proxy bearer injected by lib/tesla_api/middleware/fleet_auth.ex), typically via MyTeslaMate or Teslemetry proxies.

POLL + STREAM HYBRID (lib/teslamate/vehicles/vehicle.ex): gen_state_machine per car; polling intervals (seconds, env-overridable): asleep 30 (POLLING_ASLEEP_INTERVAL), online 60, driving 2.5, charging 5, default 15, minimum 0. With car_settings.use_streaming_api=true (default) the streaming socket delivers ~1 frame/second while driving; each frame with shift_state in D/N/R inserts one positions row via create_position(%Stream.Data{}) containing ONLY: date (ms), latitude=est_lat, longitude=est_lng, power (int kW), speed (mph->km/h rounded int), battery_level=soc, elevation (int m, from stream), odometer (km). Poll-based positions (streaming off, or non-drive inserts) carry the full column set incl. usable_battery_level, ranges, temps, climate, tpms; elevation then comes from local SRTM tiles (lib/teslamate/terrain.ex, SRTM_CACHE).

DASHCAM OVERLAY DATA AVAILABILITY: per-second during-drive telemetry lives in positions (JOIN drives ON positions.drive_id) with speed/power/battery_level/elevation/lat/lon/odometer at ~1 Hz (stream mode). HEADING IS NOT PERSISTED — positions has no heading/course column; heading (est_heading) is only merged into the live Summary and published on the MQTT 'heading' topic, so historical course must be computed from consecutive lat/lon. usable_battery_level, temps, and ranges are NULL on stream-inserted rows and only present on the sparser poll-based rows.

EXTENSION MODEL: no plugin system; companion services integrate via (1) MQTT topics (primary live-state channel; Home Assistant, ABRP bridge, Telegram bot per website/docs/projects.md), (2) direct Postgres reads/writes (Grafana datasource does this officially; TeslaMateAgile UPDATEs charging_processes.cost; TeslaMateApi serves REST from the DB), (3) the two logging suspend/resume PUT endpoints, (4) GPX export. The DB schema is the de-facto contract and migrations run automatically at startup (entrypoint.sh).

I18N: yes, Chinese is supported in the Phoenix web UI — priv/gettext contains zh_Hans and zh_Hant locales (zh_Hans/LC_MESSAGES/default.po has 167 msgids, e.g. Settings -> 设置). UI locale is negotiated per-request by Cldr.Plug.PutLocale from query param, session, or Accept-Language (lib/teslamate_web/router.ex). The GlobalSettings 'language' field ('Chinese' => 'zh' in lib/teslamate/settings/global_settings.ex) controls OSM geocoding/address language, not the UI locale. Grafana dashboards themselves are English (Grafana set to GF_USERS_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=detect).

RUNTIME CONFIG (config/runtime.exs): DATABASE_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/NAME/POOL_SIZE/TIMEOUT/SSL/IPV6 or DATABASE_SOCKET_DIR; PORT (default 4000) / HTTP_BINDING_ADDRESS (supports unix sockets); VIRTUAL_HOST, URL_PATH, CHECK_ORIGIN, SECRET_KEY_BASE, SIGNING_SALT; ENCRYPTION_KEY (required for token storage); DEFAULT_GEOFENCE; IMPORT_DIR (default 'import'); SRTM_CACHE; TZDATA_DIR.
recommendations: Integrate live state via MQTT (teslamate/cars/$car_id/#) and history via read-only Postgres queries on positions/drives/charging_processes/charges — this is exactly how all blessed community projects work; do not call TeslaMate HTTP endpoints for data (there are none) and never write to its tables except the documented cost-update pattern (charging_processes.cost).

For dashcam telemetry overlay, query positions filtered by drive_id (drives.start_date/end_date bound the video window): you get ~1 Hz speed (km/h), power (kW), battery_level, elevation, lat/lon. Compute heading client-side from successive coordinates (atan2 of deltas) because positions has no heading column; if you need true heading, capture the MQTT 'heading' topic in real time alongside the recording, or subscribe your own consumer that archives it.

Interpolate/carry-forward usable_battery_level, temperatures, and range values across stream-inserted rows — they are only present on sparse poll-based rows; treat NULLs in those columns as 'unchanged since last poll', not missing data.

Use a dedicated read-only Postgres role for companion services and expect the schema to move (migrations auto-run on every TeslaMate upgrade at container start; e.g. tokens moved to a 'private' schema, positions indexes rewritten in 2025-2026 migrations). Pin queries to columns, not to indexes or physical layout, and gate upgrades in staging.

If subscribing MQTT, set clean-session consumers to tolerate retained messages (all topics except 'healthy' are retained), key on car_id = cars.id from the DB (not VIN), and honor MQTT_NAMESPACE if the deployment sets one.

For sentry/alarm-adjacent features, rely on the MQTT sentry_mode topic (true/false, retained) — sentry status is never written to Postgres, so any historical sentry timeline must be recorded by your own MQTT archiver.

If the deployment must move off the Owner API (business fleet accounts), keep TeslaMate unforked and switch endpoints via env only: TOKEN + TESLA_API_HOST/TESLA_AUTH_HOST/TESLA_AUTH_PATH (MyTeslaMate/Teslemetry) and TESLA_WSS_HOST/TESLA_WSS_USE_VIN for reconstructed streaming; note Fleet Telemetry-based streams are coarser (>=1 min) which degrades the per-second positions density that video overlay depends on.

Chinese-market deployments work out of the box: token region auto-detection picks owner-api.vn.cloud.tesla.cn and streaming.vn.cloud.tesla.cn, and the web UI already ships zh_Hans/zh_Hant translations — send Accept-Language: zh or ?locale=zh_Hans rather than patching the UI.

ecosystem.summary: TESLAMATE CORE (verified from local clone at <repo>/teslamate, VERSION 4.1.0-dev, and github.com/teslamate-org/teslamate): Elixir/Phoenix app, 8.8k stars, actively developed (pushed 2026-08-04). Releases: 3.0.0 (2026-02-28), 3.1.0 (2026-06-07), 4.0.0 (2026-06-13), 4.0.1 (2026-06-14). CRITICAL LICENSING FACT: relicensed from MIT to AGPL-3.0 in v3.0.0 (PR #5131); README states copyleft applies to SaaS/network use and claims "If your software interacts with or relies on TeslaMate, it must be open-source" (stronger than standard AGPL interpretation — a community-relations landmine even where legally debatable). TRADEMARK.md (dated 2026-02-02, at <repo>/teslamate/TRADEMARK.md): name must be CamelCase "TeslaMate"; PROHIBITED without written consent: using TeslaMate in any product name including "[Product] for TeslaMate" for commercial/closed-source software, company/domain/social names implying official status, commercial support branding, merch; REQUIRED: any tool interfacing with TeslaMate (even via API or database) must carry disclaimer "This project is an unofficial community tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by the official TeslaMate project." Enforcement includes App Store takedowns/DMCA. ARCHITECTURE: TeslaMate polls Tesla Owner API (default, still available to individuals) or Fleet API via env overrides; writes to Postgres; publishes ~70 retained MQTT topics under teslamate/cars/$car_id/* (full table in website/docs/integrations/mqtt.md — state, location JSON, power, speed, heading, elevation, doors/windows/TPMS, charging_state, active_route JSON, service_mode, download_perc/install_perc, etc.; MQTT_NAMESPACE env inserts a namespace for multi-tenant). Official docker-compose (website/docs/installation/docker.md): 4 services — teslamate/teslamate:latest (port 4000, ENCRYPTION_KEY + DATABASE_* + MQTT_HOST, volume ./import:/opt/app/import, cap_drop all), postgres:18-trixie, teslamate/grafana:latest (port 3000, pre-provisioned with 20 official dashboards from /grafana/dashboards: overview, battery-health, charges, charging-stats, drives, drive-stats, efficiency, projected-range, vampire-drain, trip, timeline, statistics, states, updates, visited, locations, mileage, charge-level, database-info + internal/reports), eclipse-mosquitto:2 running NO-AUTH config. Other installs: NixOS (official flake), unsupported Debian/FreeBSD/Unraid, community HA addon. Advanced guides: Traefik, Apache, unix sockets, image signature verification. IMPORT: TeslaFi CSV import built-in (BETA; ./import dir, timezone selection, row-level skip + file-level resume, TESLAFI_IMPORT_VEHICLE_ID env, REINDEX positions afterward) and tesla_apiscraper import — docs in website/docs/import/. Env-var surface (website/docs/configuration/environment_variables.md): TESLA_API_HOST, TESLA_AUTH_HOST, TESLA_AUTH_PATH, TESLA_AUTH_CLIENT_ID, TESLA_WSS_HOST, TESLA_WSS_USE_VIN, TOKEN (third-party provider bearer), POLLING_* intervals, NOMINATIM_PROXY (China-relevant), DISABLE_MQTT, URL_PATH, CHECK_ORIGIN, DATABASE_SOCKET_DIR. FLEET API IN 2025/2026 (website/docs/configuration/api.md, current): TeslaMate's official position — individuals should STAY on Owner API (richer, 1s streaming); Fleet API is only mandatory for Tesla Business Fleet accounts. Tesla pay-per-use pricing effective 2025-01-01: $1/500 data requests, $1/1,000 commands, $1/50 wakes, $1/150k streaming signals, with a $10/month credit per developer account (roughly covers streaming + 100 commands + 2 wakes/day for 2 vehicles). Recommended self-hoster paths: (a) MyTeslaMate proxy — token from app.myteslamate.com/fleet, env TOKEN + TESLA_API_HOST=https://api.myteslamate.com + TESLA_AUTH_HOST same + TESLA_AUTH_PATH=/api/oauth2/v3; streaming via TESLA_WSS_HOST=wss://streaming.myteslamate.com + TESLA_WSS_USE_VIN=true (their open-source MyTeslaMate/websocket Node.js bridge replays Fleet Telemetry as old-style streaming); docs call the TeslaMate endpoint free, while myteslamate.com/developers shows pay-as-you-go credits: 500 credits=€1, 1 credit = 1 command or 150 streaming signals or 300 API calls, wake = 20 credits, daily caps configurable. (b) Teslemetry (paid, streaming incompatible with TeslaMate). (c) DIY: developer.tesla.com free plan + own public host + region-specific fleet-api.prd.{na,eu}.vn.cloud.tesla.com (China: fleet-api.prd.cn.vn.cloud.tesla.cn) + TESLA_AUTH_CLIENT_ID; commands need teslamotors/vehicle-command HTTP proxy; telemetry needs teslamotors/fleet-telemetry + GCP PubSub + MyTeslaMate/websocket. ECOSYSTEM ATTACHMENT PATTERNS — every add-on uses one of four seams, none forks TeslaMate: (1) MQTT subscribe (abrp, telegram bot, HA integration, Node-RED, MMM-Teslamate, GeoGDO); (2) read-only Postgres SQL (Grafana dashboard packs, achievements, teslamate-mcp); (3) Postgres WRITE of specific columns (TeslaMateAgile updates charging cost; addr-fix writes addresses); (4) REST via TeslaMateApi (MateDroid, t-buddy). CHINESE ECOSYSTEM (relevant to OhmyTesla): wjsall/teslamate-chinese-dashboards (145★, MIT, 45+ localized panels + 13 original dashboards, 6-source map tile switching with WGS-84→GCJ-02 conversion, time-of-use electricity pricing with historical recalc, charging-station ¥/kWh ranking, one-click deploy script); WayneJz/teslamate-addr-fix (79★, Go, MIT — fixes Nominatim blockage in China via HTTP proxy + direct DB address writes; core now also has NOMINATIM_PROXY); ciyahu/wemate (54★, WeChat push notifications, 3D vehicle visualization, trajectory playback, driving score, geofence alerts, daily/weekly reports, curl|bash installer, port 7777 web UI); yekk-me/teslamate-mytess-docker (49★, compose for Mytess iOS app); DeaglePC/TeslamateCyberUI (cyberpunk web UI). Commercial alternatives: Teslascope, Tessie (MyTeslaMate org has a tessie-to-teslamate-import repo). AGPL-3.0 compliance strategy: TeslaMate relicensed MIT→AGPLv3 in v3.0.0 (Feb 2026). Distributing or SaaS-hosting a MODIFIED TeslaMate requires publishing the modified source under AGPLv3 — so never patch the image; upstream any needed changes instead. Separate services communicating over Postgres/MQTT/HTTP are conventionally separate works (mere aggregation in a compose file), but note the README explicitly asserts 'if your software interacts with or relies on TeslaMate, it must be open-source' — if any OhmyTesla component will be closed-source, expect community/maintainer friction and consider making TeslaMate-adjacent components open source (MIT/Apache) while keeping only genuinely independent services closed.

Trademark compliance (TRADEMARK.md, Feb 2026): do NOT put 'TeslaMate' in the product name, domain, or app-store listing ('[Product] for TeslaMate' is explicitly prohibited for commercial/closed-source products); write it CamelCase in docs; include verbatim the required disclaimer 'This project is an unofficial community tool and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by the official TeslaMate project.' in README/About. 'OhmyTesla' avoids the TeslaMate mark (separate consideration: 'Tesla' is Tesla Inc.'s mark — app-store naming risk).

Extend via upstream PRs or a thin OhmyTesla service in front of it; only build a new API if you need websockets/GraphQL/multi-tenant auth it can't do.

Ship dashboards by Grafana provisioning volume mounts (jheredianet/chinese-dashboards pattern: provisioning YAML + dashboards dir) — never rebuild the teslamate/grafana image; that keeps official dashboard updates flowing.

Harden the default stack in your overlay: official compose runs mosquitto with NO auth and Grafana admin/admin — add MQTT auth, oauth2-proxy/Authelia in front of :4000 and :3000 (core supports oauth2-proxy header sizes), set CHECK_ORIGIN=true, and use MQTT_NAMESPACE if multi-car/multi-tenant.

teslaapi.summary:
TESLA DATA-SOURCE LANDSCAPE, AUGUST 2026.

(1) FLEET API. Official API at developer.tesla.com; registration is open to individual owners (personal Tesla account, no credit card, auto-approval in minutes-to-hours). Setup requires: create app on developer dashboard (name/description/redirect URI/OAuth scopes), host your app public key at https://<your-domain>/.well-known/appspecific/com.tesla.3p.public-key.pem, then pair a "virtual key" to the car via https://tesla.com/_ak/<your-domain> (approved in the Tesla mobile app). 2021+ vehicles require signed commands via the Vehicle Command Protocol; Tesla ships an HTTP signing proxy in teslamotors/vehicle-command. Billing (pay-per-use, effective Jan 1 2025, still current mid-2026): Streaming Signals 150,000/$1 (~$0.0000067 ea), Commands 1,000/$1 ($0.001), Data (vehicle_data polls) 500/$1 ($0.002), Wakes 50/$1 ($0.02). Every developer account gets a $10/month credit — Tesla says this roughly covers "data streaming, 100 commands, and 2 wakes per day for two vehicles". The old free "Discovery tier" (2023) was superseded by this credit model. Note asymmetry: polling vehicle_data is ~300x costlier per datum than telemetry signals; 1-min polling ≈ $0.12/hr of driving. vehicle_data endpoint takes ?endpoints=... (semicolon-separated) with groups: charge_state, climate_state, closures_state, drive_state, gui_settings, location_data (lat/lon moved here in 2023.38+ firmware — drive_state no longer returns coordinates without it), vehicle_config, vehicle_state, vehicle_data_combo. Other key endpoints: /wake_up, command endpoints (must be routed through the signed-command proxy for modern cars). Rate limiting exists (TeslaMate handles Fleet API EXCEEDED_LIMIT with 15-min backoff). REGIONS: NA, EU, and China. China is a fully separate universe: separate portal developer.tesla.cn (requires tesla.cn account + a +86 phone number), separate base URL https://fleet-api.prd.cn.vn.cloud.tesla.cn, docs at developer.tesla.cn/docs/fleet-api. Third-party bridges (e.g. Tessie) advertise automatic NA/EU/China routing.

(2) FLEET TELEMETRY (github.com/teslamotors/fleet-telemetry, Go, 874 stars, pushed 2026-07-15, actively maintained). Server reference implementation of Tesla's vehicle→server push protocol: vehicles open a persistent mTLS WebSocket to your server and push protobuf frames. Self-host requirements: FQDN + valid TLS cert with mTLS termination, public key at the .well-known path, virtual key paired, per-vehicle config pushed via fleet_telemetry_config endpoint (fields + interval_seconds each), firmware ≥2023.20.6 (older Model S/X unsupported until ~2025.20; as of July 2025 effectively all vehicles supported). Dispatchers: Kafka (preferred), Kinesis, Google Pub/Sub, ZMQ, MQTT, Redis Pub/Sub, stdout logger. Streams: V (vehicle data), alerts, errors, plus optional connectivity events (proxy for online/asleep state). Field catalog ~407 fields (protos/vehicle_data.proto); notable: Location(21), GpsState(22), GpsHeading(23), VehicleSpeed(4), Soc(8), BatteryLevel(42), EstBatteryRange(40), Odometer(5), Gear(10), DetailedChargeState(179) (enum Disconnected/NoPower/Starting/Charging/Complete/Stopped), ACChargingPower(37)/DCChargingPower(35), ChargeLimitSoc(38), TimeToFullCharge(43), InsideTemp(85)/OutsideTemp(86), Locked(59), DoorState(58) (Doors msg: DriverFront/DriverRear/PassengerFront/PassengerRear/TrunkFront/TrunkRear), SENTRYMODE(65) with enum SentryModeState: Off/Idle/Armed/AWARE/PANIC/Quiet — SentryModeStateAware/Panic are the alarm-relevant transitions; also ServiceMode(159), ValetModeEnabled(226), PinToDriveEnabled(124), GuestModeEnabled(123), TpmsHard/SoftWarnings(224/225), ForwardCollisionWarning(130), LocatedAtHome/Work/Favorite. There is NO dedicated "sentry event with camera/reason" signal — SentryMode state changes are the closest realtime security telemetry. Minimum interval is 1s for most fields (Location, VehicleSpeed, Soc, SentryMode, Gear, DetailedChargeState all min 1s; Odometer 10s; limits/defaults enumerable at api.teslemetry.com/fields.json). Latency: push over persistent WebSocket, effectively ~1–2s end-to-end when the car is online (vehicle transmits at the configured cadence; one integrator reports ~500ms internal send cadence). Billing: streaming signals are billed by Tesla per-signal even to a self-hosted server (the repo ships signal-count metrics explicitly "to identify approximate billing", incl. per-VIN tracking) — but at 150k signals/$1, ~5 fields at 10s intervals is ~$0.86/mo/car, easily inside the $10 credit; Location@1s continuous while driving ≈ 100k signals/mo ≈ $0.72.

(3) LEGACY OWNER API (owner-api.teslamotors.com): zombie but alive for individuals in Aug 2026. Officially shut down for Business Fleet accounts (their cars return errors pointing to Fleet API); for individual consumer accounts it still works, including the old 1 Hz driving-telemetry WebSocket stream (streaming.vetted... "streaming API"), which TeslaMate 4.x still uses by default. Tesla has been tightening it: auth now requires TLS1.2+/HTTP2 (a June 2026 change briefly broke TeslaMate until a patched release), commands rejected on some vehicles, no announced end date for individuals but consensus is it can die any time. 2020-and-older Model S/X don't support the new streaming replacement, complicating migration.

(4) BLE — teslamotors/vehicle-command (Go, 685 stars, pushed 2026-07-31, active). Implements the Vehicle Command Protocol over both Fleet API REST and direct BLE. tesla-keygen creates a NIST P-256 key; enroll via `tesla-control -ble add-key-request public_key.pem owner cloud_key` + NFC-card tap on console; thereafter most commands (lock/unlock, climate, charging, trunk, wake) work purely locally over BLE with zero Fleet API involvement and ZERO fees, no internet. Does not run on Windows (Go BLE library limitation); Linux/BlueZ (incl. Raspberry Pi) and macOS work. Wake over BLE works (this is how esphome-tesla-ble and similar keep cars controllable without paying $0.02/wake). BLE gives commands, not telemetry streams (limited state reads only). Range = Bluetooth (~5–20m), so it suits home/garage automation, not remote alerts.

(5) TESLACAM USB FORMAT. Drive must be exFAT (Tesla-formatted: 128KB clusters); root folder TeslaCam/ with RecentClips/ (flat rolling ~1hr dashcam buffer, oldest auto-deleted), SavedClips/ and SentryClips/ (each event = subfolder named YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS containing up to ~10 min of pre-event footage). Files: one MP4 per camera per minute, named YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS-<camera>.mp4 with camera ∈ {front, back, left_repeater, right_repeater} on HW3 (4 cams) and additionally {left_pillar, right_pillar} on HW4 (6 cams; B-pillar recording shipped in 2025.14 "Spring Update", HW4-only — HW3 cars, even Ryzen-infotainment ones, never got it). Event folders contain event.json + thumb.png. event.json schema: {"timestamp":"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS" (local), "city":"<name>", "est_lat":"<string>", "est_lon":"<string>", "reason":"<code>", "camera":"<digit string>"}. Observed reason codes: sentry_aware_object_detection, sentry_aware_accel_<value>, user_interaction_dashcam_icon_tapped, user_interaction_dashcam_panel_save, user_interaction_honk (sentry panic events also occur). camera numbering (community-reverse-engineered, treat cautiously — mappings differ between tools): 0=front, 1=fisheye, 2=narrow, 3=left_repeater, 4=right_repeater, 5=left B-pillar, 6=right B-pillar, 7=rear, 8=cabin. Codecs/resolutions actually observed: HW3 = 1280x960 all cameras, historically H.264 ~36fps, newer firmware HEVC/H.265 (players must handle both); HW4 = front 2896x1876, other cameras 1448x938, HEVC, ~24–30fps (front fps dropped vs HW3). ~15–30MB per camera-minute; a HW4 minute = 6 files. Quirks: clips are ~59s with 2–3s gaps between consecutive minute files; per-camera files for the same minute can differ slightly in length/start (align by filename timestamp + frame offsets, not by container timestamps); MP4 moov atom is written last, so the in-progress/last minute at power-cut is often corrupt/unplayable (recoverable by carving); burned-in on-video timestamps have historically been wrong (hardcoded Pacific in some firmwares) — FILENAME timestamps are the trustworthy clock; slow USB drives cause dropped/corrupt segments.

(6) CHINA. Chinese cars DO have Dashcam/TeslaCam and Sentry Mode; Tesla China's official position (Aug 2023, after sentry-related parking bans): Sentry/dashcam footage is stored ONLY on the local USB drive, never uploaded, and remote live-camera viewing from the app is disabled in China. All Chinese vehicle cloud data is stored in-country (Shanghai data center) per PIPL/data-security rules. Fleet API exists in China as a separate region: developer.tesla.cn portal (+86 phone required), base URL fleet-api.prd.cn.vn.cloud.tesla.cn; a self-hosted Chinese user must register there, and a self-hosted fleet-telemetry server for a Chinese car should be hosted reachable from China (data-residency argues for hosting in-country; also GFW reliability). BLE vehicle-command is region-independent (protocol lives in the car) and should work in China. TeslaCam USB parsing is 100% offline/local — zero regulatory or connectivity exposure, identical format worldwide.

TESLAMATE CONTEXT (local repo = 4.1.0-dev): still Owner-API-first with optional Fleet API via bring-your-own token or proxies; publishes rich MQTT topics (now incl. service_mode, window/sunroof states, software update progress); handles Fleet API rate limits. Proxy ecosystem: MyTeslaMate is no longer free (500 credits/€1; 1 command=1cr, 150 signals=1cr, 300 API calls=1cr, wake=20cr; includes fleet-telemetry→MQTT bridging and even "Sentry break-in alerts via Telegram" — a direct competitor feature); Teslemetry repositioned as paid Fleet API access layer (webhooks/SSE, fields.json catalog).

feature_ideas: Realtime Sentry alert pipeline: subscribe to Fleet Telemetry SentryMode field (1s min interval) and fire a push/Telegram alert on transition to SentryModeStateAware or SentryModeStatePanic — MyTeslaMate already sells 'Sentry break-in alerts via Telegram', proving demand; a self-hosted version differentiates OhmyTesla

Six-camera synchronized player that handles both HW3 (4 cams, 1280x960) and HW4 (6 cams incl. left_pillar/right_pillar, 2896x1876 front) layouts, both H.264 and HEVC, and tolerates the 59s+2-3s-gap chunking and per-camera misalignment

Telemetry-on-video overlay: join TeslaMate positions (1Hz stream) or Fleet Telemetry Location/VehicleSpeed/Soc (1s) onto TeslaCam clips using filename timestamps as the master clock, with a per-car configurable clock-offset calibration step to absorb drift
Corrupt-clip triage: detect moov-atom-missing MP4s (power-cut last minute), flag or carve-recover them instead of failing playback
Sentry event ↔ telemetry correlation: when an event.json appears, pull the surrounding SentryMode/Location/Locked telemetry window to show what the car sensed before/after
BLE quick actions from the OhmyTesla host (Raspberry Pi/Mac in garage): lock, climate, wake via vehicle-command with zero Fleet API fees
Zero-cost mode: run entirely from TeslaMate MQTT + USB TeslaCam ingestion with no Tesla developer account at all; offer Fleet Telemetry as an opt-in upgrade sized to stay under the $10/month credit

China mode: developer.tesla.cn/fleet-api.prd.cn.vn.cloud.tesla.cn region switch, no reliance on remote live-camera (disabled in China), all TeslaCam processing local to comply with data-residency expectations
recommendations: (a) Realtime alerts: build on Fleet Telemetry, not polling. SentryMode(65) at 1s interval plus connectivity events gives ~1–2s push latency; a sentry-focused field set costs well under the $10/month Tesla credit (150k signals/$1). Accept telemetry either from a self-hosted fleet-telemetry server (FQDN+mTLS+virtual key, more setup) or via a proxy's MQTT bridge. Do NOT build alerts on vehicle_data polling ($0.002/poll, high latency) or on the Owner API (can die without notice).

(b) Overlay sync accuracy: master clock = TeslaCam filename timestamps (burned-in video timestamps are unreliable, historically hardcoded Pacific). Sync source ranking: TeslaMate positions from the 1Hz Owner-API stream today; design the ingestion behind an interface so Fleet Telemetry Location@1s can replace it when the Owner API dies. Handle the known 2–3s inter-minute gaps and per-camera offsets; provide a one-time user calibration (slide overlay ±N seconds) per car.

(c) Zero-additional-cost operation: consume TeslaMate's MQTT topics (location, speed, soc, sentry, locked, service_mode) + direct USB TeslaCam parsing — no Tesla developer account, no fees, works today. For users who outlive the Owner API, the documented upgrade path is their own free Fleet API app whose $10 credit covers a 1–2 car telemetry config, plus BLE vehicle-command for fee-free local commands/wakes.

Architectural: treat data sources as pluggable adapters (OwnerAPI-via-TeslaMate | FleetTelemetry-self-hosted | FleetTelemetry-via-proxy | USB-TeslaCam), because the Owner API is a zombie, proxies keep changing pricing (MyTeslaMate dropped its free tier), and Tesla's per-signal billing rewards narrow field sets.

China: ship a region flag. Chinese users need developer.tesla.cn (+86 phone) and fleet-api.prd.cn.vn.cloud.tesla.cn; remote live camera is disabled there but Sentry/TeslaCam USB recording works identically, so the USB-ingestion path is the China-safe core. Keep all video processing local (data-residency + user trust).

TeslaCam ingestion hard requirements: exFAT reading, HEVC decode (HW4 and newer HW3 firmware), 2896x1876 front streams (transcode/downscale for web playback), tolerate missing/corrupt moov-atom clips, HW3 4-cam vs HW4 6-cam layout detection from filename suffixes, and treat event.json camera numbering as heuristic (verify against real HW4 data).
